audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.72%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.4%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dell'0.57%, il VIX è salito dello 0.3%. Il dollaro si è mosso poco, con il DXY in aumento dello 0.03%. L'oro è salito dello 0.43%, raggiungendo i 4349.4 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è in rialzo dello 0.41%, a 79.28 dollari. I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani sono saliti, con il US 10Y Yield in aumento dello 0.54%, al 4.48%.

La Banca del Giappone ha aumentato i tassi d'interesse, mentre il vice capo avverte di rischi d'inflazione e incertezze legate all'Iran. L'Unione Europea è in attesa delle mosse della Fed, con gli investitori che stanno accumulando scommesse rialziste sul dollaro.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
  Bitcoin scende del 2,56% a 64.859 dollari. I flussi degli ETF mostrano un deflusso di 10,5 milioni di dollari. 
  Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalla generale avversione al rischio degli investitori. 
  Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantaquattromila dollari, ma la discesa potrebbe proseguire. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende dell'1,09% a mille settecentosettantuno dollari, Solana perde il 3,06% a settantadue virgola quarantasette dollari e BNB scende del 2,19% a seiccentouno virgola sessantasei dollari. 
  L'indice Fear & Greed scende a 22, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.72%, Shanghai up 0.4%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.57%, the VIX rose 0.3%. The dollar moved little, with the DXY up 0.03%. Gold rose 0.43%, reaching $4,349.4 an ounce. Oil is up 0.41%, at $79.28 US Treasury yields rose, with the US 10Y Yield up 0.54%, to 4.48%. The Bank of Japan raised interest rates, while the deputy governor warns of inflation risks and uncertainties related to Iran. The European Union is waiting for the Fed's moves, with investors accumulating bullish bets on the dollar. No major macroeconomic data out today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin falls 2.56% to $64,859 ETF flows show an outflow of $10.5 million. This movement could be influenced by the general risk aversion of investors. Bitcoin holds above sixty-four thousand dollars, but the decline could continue. Among altcoins, Ethereum falls 1.09% to $1,771, Solana loses 3.06% to $72.47 and BNB falls 2.19% to $601.66 The Fear & Greed index drops to 22, in Extreme Fear zone, suggests caution on investors. No macro data on the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's themes, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Bond yield responses to macro news: the role of macro forecast disagreement and monetary policy uncertainty
articles.snippet: by Peter Hördahl, Burçin Kısacıkoğlu, Dora Xia Bond yields react to macroeconomic surprises, but the magnitude of this responsiveness depends on macroeconomic forecast disagreement and monetary policy uncertainty. Using intraday responses of US Treasury futures to surprises in macroeconomic data releases, we find that greater forecast disagreement about an economic indicator prior to its release dampens the yield curve response, while higher monetary policy uncertainty amplifies it. An exception is inflation surprises: prior to the post-COVID inflation surge, bond yield reactions to inflation surprises were not amplified by monetary policy uncertainty.

articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. articles.title: Cyber insurance unpacked: the corporate digital safety net
articles.snippet: In a more digitalised and interconnected world, cyber risk is increasingly recognised as a significant threat to economic and financial stability. The rapid evolution of cyber threats driven by technological advances, including artificial intelligence (AI), rising geopolitical tensions and the interconnected nature of digital ecosystems, is increasing the speed, scale, sophistication and systemic nature of both malicious and non-malicious cyber incidents.

articles.title: Oil Prices Crash as Traders Bet the War Is Over
articles.snippet: The oil market just did something remarkable. After spending months pricing in tanker attacks, shut-in production, damaged LNG facilities, and the largest supply disruption in modern oil market history, traders are suddenly betting the crisis is ending. Brent crude futures fell below $79 per barrel on Tuesday, its lowest level since March, after the United States and Iran digitally signed a peace agreement that includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the immediate return of Iranian oil sales to global markets. The selloff has been relentless.…

articles.title: VanEck: Bitcoin Miners Face $50B Funding Gap as AI Pivot Separates Winners From Losers
articles.snippet: Bitcoin Magazine VanEck: Bitcoin Miners Face $50B Funding Gap as AI Pivot Separates Winners From Losers VanEck says Bitcoin miners pursuing AI data center businesses face a roughly $50 billion funding gap, with investors increasingly rewarding companies that have already secured and energized AI infrastructure capacity while punishing those still relying on unproven pipeline projections. This post VanEck: Bitcoin Miners Face $50B Funding Gap as AI Pivot Separates Winners From Losers first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .
